content.text:
I only looked at your Vercel account and changed nothing. Below is what I found and the alerts I'd set up. You decide which ones to turn on.

## What your project looks like today (`your-family-farmer`, Pro)

- **Usage this cycle (Oct 16 – Nov 16):** $0.77 so far, which is 4% of the $20 monthly credit that comes with Pro.
- **Requests:** about 3,000–6,000 a day on production. There were **zero 5xx errors in the last 7 days**: 404s were around 25 a day and 403s around 10 a day.
- **Deployments:** the last 40 had no production failures. 4 preview builds failed.
- **Firewall:** there is no config at all, so no custom rules and bot protection is off. On Oct 21, DDoS mitigation alone blocked 952 requests in one day.
- **Spend limit:** my notes from Oct 21 say the budget is $200 with auto-pause off. The API would not show it to me today, so please check it on the dashboard.
- **Image optimisation:** 3.03K transformations so far this cycle. The fix that turns this off reached prod only on Oct 26, so this number should stop growing now. This is the counter that paused your site on Oct 15.

## Recommended alerts, most important first

| # | Alert | Threshold | On Pro? | Where |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Spend Management budget** | Lower it from $200 to **$50**. Notify at 50%, 75% and 100%. | ✅ Free | Team Settings → Billing → Spend Management |
| 2 | **Pause projects at 100% of budget** | My advice: **keep it OFF** for production. A paused site loses more than $50. | ✅ Free | Same page |
| 3 | **Failed production deployment** | Email and web notification on every failure | ✅ Free | Account Settings → Notifications |
| 4 | **Usage notifications** for image transformations, function invocations and data transfer | Default emails at 50%, 75% and 100% of included usage | ✅ Free (sent to the team owner) | Notifications, plus the Usage page |
| 5 | **Bot protection** (managed ruleset) | Turn on in "Log" mode for 3 days, then switch to "Challenge" | ✅ Free | Project → Firewall → Bot Management |
| 6 | **Rate limit on `/api/otp/send`** | For example, 5 requests per 10 minutes per IP | ✅ Pro includes some free rate-limit rules | Project → Firewall → Custom rule |
| 7 | **5xx error spike / function failures** | Alert if there are more than 20 5xx in 15 minutes, or more than 1% of requests are 5xx | ⚠️ Vercel's own anomaly alerts need **Observability Plus** (paid add-on). Please check pricing on your dashboard before turning it on. | Observability → Alerts |
| 8 | **Uptime check** on `gogrameen.in` and one API route | Check every 5 minutes, alert after 2 failures in a row | ❌ Vercel does not have this. Use a free external service such as UptimeRobot or Better Stack. | Outside Vercel |
| 9 | **Cron failure** for `/api/cron/reconcile-payments` (runs daily at 02:00 UTC) | Alert if it doesn't succeed once in 24 hours | ❌ Vercel does not alert on cron failures. Use a free heartbeat monitor, or have the cron send a WhatsApp message when it fails. | Small code change |

## Why these thresholds

- **$50 budget:** your real usage is about $1 a month. With $200, an attack could burn $150+ before you hear anything. With $50, the first email comes at about $25.
- **#6 is the biggest money risk, and it is not a Vercel cost.** Every OTP send costs you a WhatsApp message. The current rate limit in `rate-limit.ts` is kept in memory on each server instance, so a bot spread across several instances is only weakly blocked. A firewall rule blocks it before your code even runs.
- **5xx threshold:** you have 0 errors a day today. Even 20 in 15 minutes means something is really broken, such as a Supabase outage or a bad deploy, and it won't fire on noise.
- **Pause off:** your site was already paused once (Oct 15, image overage). For a marketplace, being down is worse than a small overage, so I'd rely on the emails instead.

## What needs your approval before I do anything

1. Lowering the budget to $50 (free, dashboard)
2. Bot protection in Log mode, plus an OTP rate-limit rule (free, I can set these up with `vercel firewall` if you say yes)
3. Whether to buy Observability Plus for #7 (paid, so only if you want it)
4. A heartbeat check for the cron job (small code change on staging, with tests)

Items 1, 3 and 4 in the main table (budget, failed-deployment emails, usage emails) are dashboard clicks only you can make. Tell me which of the four above to set up and I'll do them one by one.

That setup is fine. You can click **Save**.

- **$30 is even tighter than the $50 I suggested, and that's okay.** This budget only counts usage beyond the $20 monthly credit. Your usage is about $1 a month, so with $30 the first email comes at $15 of extra spend. Normal traffic will never reach it, but a bot attack or something like the Oct 15 image problem will.
- **"Current spend $0"** is correct. All your usage so far is covered by the $20 credit.
- **Leave "Pause production deployments" OFF.** If you hit the budget, you get an email and the site stays up for buyers and farmers.
- **Leave the webhook empty.** The 50%, 75% and 100% emails go to the team owner's email anyway. We can add a webhook later if you want these alerts on WhatsApp.

After saving, the next free items are:

1. **Failed-deployment emails**: Account Settings → Notifications. Tick "Deployment failed" for production.
2. **Bot protection in Log mode, plus a rate limit on `/api/otp/send`**: just say yes and I'll set these up with the CLI.

content.text:
**Short answer: Vercel costs nothing, but right now the farmer gets an error message instead of the photo being uploaded.**

## What happens today
In the farmer dashboard (`src/app/farmer/dashboard/page.tsx`, the produce, profile and harvest photo pickers):
- **Photo over 8 MB → rejected** with "Image must be under 8 MB." A 10 MB photo is blocked.
- **Photo under 8 MB → compressed on the phone** to 1200px JPEG (`src/lib/imageCompress.ts`), which comes out at roughly 150–300 KB, and then uploaded.

## Effect on cost
- **Vercel: ₹0.** Photos go from the phone **directly to Supabase Storage**, not through Vercel. Buyers also load photos straight from Supabase, since image optimisation is off. So photo size can never cause another Vercel pause.
- **Supabase:** only the compressed ~200 KB file is stored, so this is fine.

## Problems I found
1. **Bad experience for farmers:** some new phones (50MP/108MP cameras) take 10–20 MB photos. Since we compress anyway, we should **compress first and only then check the size**. A 10 MB photo would then upload fine as ~200 KB.
2. **The moderator listing form (`src/app/moderator/listings/ListingForm.tsx`) doesn't compress at all and has no size check.** A moderator uploading a 10 MB photo stores it at full size, and every buyer then downloads 10 MB on 4G. That makes the page very slow and uses Supabase bandwidth.
3. **The `farm-images` bucket has no file-size limit.** It's anon-write, so anyone with the public key could upload huge files directly and fill your storage. A bucket limit (for example 2 MB, images only) blocks that on the Supabase side.

## Suggested fix (staging first, with tests)
- Compress first, then check, in all photo pickers. A 10 MB photo is then accepted and becomes ~200 KB.
- Add compression to the moderator ListingForm.
- One SQL line: set `file_size_limit = 2MB` and `allowed_mime_types = image/*` on `farm-images`. You'd run it on staging first, then on prod, and I'll add it to `staging-schema.sql`.
